A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMSC dataset and debiasing approach. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated results and renamed methods.

before.justification: V1 reports original debiasing experiments, image-distribution measurements, component ablations, and supplementary cross-dataset evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds CMSC-trained comparisons, component-tuning experiments, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: ASD is renamed CSD, but the instance-level Skew selection, resampling algorithm, and exponential loss weighting remain unchanged. Full-parameter fine-tuning is newly explained, without evidence that the proposed debiasing procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use CMSC, SocialCounterfactuals, FairFace, VQAv2, MMBench, and TextVQA, with the same CMSC concepts and demographic categories. The added tuning variants and human judgments evaluate retained task coverage; they do not establish a new domain or input population.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 adds an evaluated LoRA comparison and language-only/vision-only tuning controls. Figure 5 removes the direct fine-tuning comparator from the race-specific comparison. FT and POPE remain in the main benchmark tables.

E3.justification: V2 introduces CMSC-trained main comparisons instead of v1's SocialCounterfactuals-trained main setting, retaining the latter in Table S6. It also adds component-tuning and human-choice protocols. Generation templates and the appendix's filtering/P2P order are substantively revised as documented procedures; the PDFs do not establish whether existing images were regenerated.

E4.justification: V2 adds a limited investigation of full versus component-only and LoRA tuning, plus qualitative examples and a brief preference study (Appendices A.1 and C.2, Figure S4). Existing loss/resampling, learning-rate, race-specific, and cross-subset analyses largely remain, although some settings and results change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's percentage annotations and 85% preference result do not introduce uncertainty estimation; the Skew boxplots describe distributions across concepts and attributes.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial CMSC-trained results in Tables 3–4, including LLaVA-13B CSD versus FT MinSkew@C of -0.8167 versus -1.5107 on CMSC. These are different-setting results, not improvements over v1's SocialCounterfactuals-trained scores, which remain unchanged in Table S6. LoRA/component-tuning results and 85% human preference are also new.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Skew aggregation, autoregressive objective, resampling formulas, and weighted loss in Equations 1–13 remain equivalent. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an 18-concept counterfactual dataset and bias-aware resampling/loss weighting that reduce bias while preserving general capabilities. Revised numerical examples support these retained claims. The change from 'three' to 'four' architectures does not add a model configuration: both already evaluate LLaVA-7B/13B, Qwen-VL-7B, and Bunny-8B.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explains why biases spanning language and vision motivate full-model tuning. It also develops a substantive defense against SDXL-generated bias, attributing control to filtering and prompts, and explicitly limits the target to demographic attribute–concept associations rather than other content biases. These arguments and applicability boundaries are absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 substantially revises generation templates and specifies GPT-4o prompt variation, CLIP-based filtering, three-expert voting, full-parameter tuning, and a common evaluation prompt. Conversely, it omits v1's SocialCounterfactuals 80/20 split, Qwen learning rate, and 30 warm-up steps. LLaVA/Bunny learning rates remain in the appendix; no code/data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting sociology and fairness references, including GenderBias-VL, VLBiasBench, and test-time visual attribute steering, while removing some background citations. The data-based/objective-based organization and claimed positioning remain largely unchanged; these citations are not additional evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, dataset-generation explanation, and supplementary prompts; renames ASD to CSD; reorganizes evaluation and experimental-settings sections; and restructures the appendix around motivation, construction, and experiments. Author/affiliation information and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: Several central plots are redrawn, recolored, and annotated. Figure 5 removes FT groups and introduces nonzero horizontal-axis minima; Figure 6 gains an outlier legend. Tables 2 and 4 are reformatted, Table S1 and Figure S4 are added, and the former main Table 3 moves to Table S6. The 18 concept image galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 more directly validates the combined CMSC/CSD contribution through CMSC-trained comparisons while preserving earlier main results, and adds useful generation details and tuning analyses. These gains are limited by lost reproducibility settings, an undocumented user-study sample size, and a new reporting error: Section 6.3.1 attributes -0.6193 to Qwen+Resample, whereas Table 4 reports -0.7414 and assigns -0.6193 to CSD.
